chunks: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about exchanging one slave for two slaves, and one slave for another slave along with dirhams, so he said:
There is no harm in all kinds of animals [being exchanged] hand to hand.

key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمِ: dirhams; coined silver money included alongside an exchanged slave
key_terms.الْحَيَوَانِ: animals; the broader legal category under which the ruling is expressed
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ: a slave; the item being exchanged in the transaction
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression of legal permissibility
key_terms.يَدًا بِيَدٍ: hand to hand; immediate spot exchange without delay

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to exchange one slave for two slaves or with dirhams in a hand-to-hand transaction?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning barter exchange involving slaves, classifying them under the broader category of animals for purposes of immediate exchange. The Imam عليه السلام permits such exchange when it is conducted hand to hand, indicating spot exchange without deferment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4009 - Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah asked Abu Abdullah (as) about exchanging one slave for two slaves, or one slave for another slave along with dirhams.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in exchanging all types of animals hand-to-hand."
